title: Conjecture 4
context_text: For a graph $G$ and an integer $k$, the ($k$-)configuration graph $\mathcal{R}_k(G)$ has the independent sets of size $k$ of $G$ as vertices, two of them being adjacent if one is obtained from the other by a token jump, i.e. by removing one vertex and adding another vertex (Token Jumping model). $D(n,k)$ is the maximum, over all $n$-vertex graphs $G$, of the diameter of a connected component of $\mathcal{R}_k(G)$, i.e. the maximum length of a shortest reconfiguration sequence between two $k$-independent sets. The authors prove $D(n,k)\le\binom{n}{k-1}$, $D(n,2)=n-2$ (the complement of the path being the unique extremal graph), and, via the hypergraph removal lemma, $D(n,k)=o(n^{k-1})$ for $k\ge3$; their lower bounds also hold for Token Sliding. For $k=3$ they give an almost tight construction $D(n,3)\ge n^2/e^{O(\sqrt{\log n})}$ (related to the $(6,3)$-problem and built from 3-AP-free sets), and in general $D(n,k)\ge n^{2\lfloor k/3\rfloor}/e^{O_k(\sqrt{\log n})}$. They could not show that lower and upper bounds almost match for $k\ge4$: in particular it is open whether the 4-configuration graph can have super-quadratic diameter, while the upper bound is $o(n^3)$. As a first step towards super-quadratic diameter one needs many copies of $K_4$ no two sharing a triangle, and Gowers and Janzer showed that there are $n$-vertex graphs with $n^{k-1-o(1)}$ copies of $K_k$ such that every $K_{k-1}$ lies in at most one of them, which might suggest $D(n,k)=n^{k-1-o(1)}$ in general.

title: Question 8
statement_text: What is the asymptotic behavior of $\max_k D(n, k)$?
context_text: For a graph $G$ and an integer $k$, the ($k$-)configuration graph $\mathcal{R}_k(G)$ has the independent sets of size $k$ of $G$ as vertices, two of them being adjacent if one is obtained from the other by a token jump, i.e. by removing one vertex and adding another vertex (Token Jumping model). $D(n,k)$ is the maximum, over all $n$-vertex graphs $G$, of the diameter of a connected component of $\mathcal{R}_k(G)$, i.e. the maximum length of a shortest reconfiguration sequence between two $k$-independent sets. The authors prove $D(n,k)\le\binom{n}{k-1}$, $D(n,2)=n-2$ (the complement of the path being the unique extremal graph), and, via the hypergraph removal lemma, $D(n,k)=o(n^{k-1})$ for $k\ge3$; their lower bounds also hold for Token Sliding. The asymptotic lower bounds they prove for fixed $k$ (such as $D(n,k)\ge n^{2\lfloor k/3\rfloor}/e^{O_k(\sqrt{\log n})}$) may fail when $k$ grows with $n$. Building on a construction from the CoRe Challenge 2022, they show that there are graphs on $10n$ vertices whose configuration graph for independent sets of size $3n$ is a path of length $\Theta(4^n)$, and more generally that $D(n,k)=\Omega(2^{n/5})$ for every $k$ with $3n/10\le k\le2n/5$; they find it surprising that this exponential bound holds for such a range of $k$, which raises the question of the maximum over $k$.
